topics.title: Noble's walk-through
topics.intro: From Noble's walk-through (2026-10-15) and your notes after it: 102 points in docs/comp-report/feedback/2026-10-15-noble/, one report per topic, and Dispatches 15–24. Each question has a recommended default, so the dispatches build on it unless you object. Read the topic reports alongside: each question cites its NW ids.

questions.q: What is the offer target: one number, or a range?
questions.short: The target: one number or a range
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble could not tell what the target means (NW-002): for a buyer, the most the client would pay, or what they hope to pay.

Why it needs you. It never moves a number; it is a named price, hidden from the writer and out of the email. A relabel fixes the confusion with a copy change. A range toggle touches the saved target, Findings' marker and QA, and needs a Findings design (it can go to Claude Design with NW-064).

Waits for you. The relabel is built only on an A answer (Dispatch 20).
options: buyer: "Most your client would pay"; seller: "Price you want to justify". Copy only
buyer and seller; waits for the Findings design

questions.q: How should the tool model HDFC, sponsor units, condops, townhouses and houses?
questions.short: Property types beyond condo and co-op
questions.context:
What this is about. The report's type is only condo or co-op, and it drives the pricing (NW-018 a, NW-019). Noble hit HDFC, sponsor units and a townhouse.

Why it needs you. Sponsor and HDFC are attributes of a co-op or condo sale, not separate pricing methods, and the listing read already returns both. A: no migration and no engine change. B: a migration plus a pricing answer for each new type. Townhouses and whole houses wait on a pricing answer either way.

Waits for you. The type model (NW-018 a) is built only on an A answer (Dispatch 16).
options: Keep condo or co-op as the pricing basis
add a type label (HDFC, condop, townhouse, house) with sponsor and HDFC as flags
Widen the report type and the engine
migration and a pricing rule per type

questions.q: Photos in the Designed email: linked from StreetEasy, or copied and hosted by Casa?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble wants listing photos (NW-020, NW-058). The home and Sort will show them from StreetEasy's image URLs either way.

Why it needs you. The design of record says linked, not hosted ({repo}/docs/comp-report/01-design.md). Linking needs no storage and no new public route. The risk is an image going blank when a listing is pulled. Hosting copies needs Blobs and a public unguessable route.
options: revisit if blanks show up in sent emails
Store copies in Blobs at copy time
served from a public unguessable route

questions.q: Which word for a unit that is well kept but not redone: "Good" or "Well kept"?
questions.short: Condition scale: the word for Good
questions.context:
What this is about. The new condition scale is Needs work, Original, Good, Updated, Renovated, Mint, with an ⓘ on each (NW-012).

Why it needs you. It is the label agents see for a middle step. "Good" is already a stored state and the design's word. "Like new" sits too close to Mint.

questions.q: What do agents call a tag?
questions.context:
What this is about. "Tag" confused Noble (NW-028, NW-040, NW-047). The word changes in the Needs line, the readiness line, the card, the edit form and the filter.

Why it needs you. The list holds differences (smaller, lower floor, no outdoor space) as well as similarities, so "Similarity tags" would be wrong half the time.

questions.q: Does starring a comp also make it 1st tier?
questions.context:
What this is about. The ★ moves into the tier control as a fourth segment (NW-026).

Why it needs you. Today a 2nd-tier or excluded comp can be the one the email leads with. Making ★ set 1st (and picking 2nd or ✕ clear it) removes that, and matches how you already treat anchoring as a kind of tiering.
options: ★ sets 1st; picking 2nd or ✕ clears the star
★ stays independent of tier, as today

questions.q: How does a StreetEasy fact the agent unlocks and overrides count?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble wants to fix a wrong floor or size on an export comp. Today those facts are locked (NW-044). The build adds a lock per fact; unlocking overrides it.

Why it needs you. It decides whether the override moves the numbers as a fact or lands only in the "with estimates" figures. The use is correcting StreetEasy's mistakes, and StreetEasy's value stays on record in "Where it came from".

questions.q: Are a note and tags both required on every comp?
questions.context:
What this is about. Sort's "Needs tier, note, tag" blocks Findings until all are done (NW-046).

Why it needs you. The note is the learning part for new agents. Experienced ones may find both a chore. The practice and full levels already exist (D-11, D-27).

Waits for you. Built only on an A answer: it changes D-27's Save rule (Dispatch 15).
options: Practice agents need both; full agents need tags, note optional
A note only when a comp has no tags

questions.q: Tags the data already settles: pre-fill, or suggest?
questions.context:
What this is about. Same building, first floor, 6+ months, new development and the size scale can be worked out from the data (NW-059). Contradicting tags (an outdoor pick vs "No outdoor space") clear on their own.

Why it needs you. Tags are the agent's. A pre-filled tag would satisfy "needs a tag" with no thought behind it.
options: Suggest as one-click chips marked "from the data"
Pre-fill for full agents, suggest for practice agents

questions.q: The size scale: where do Smaller, Similar and Bigger start?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble wants Size as an ordered scale with one choice (NW-045). The engine only flags size past 25%.

Why it needs you. Someone has to name the bands. They stay house-method configuration, so Noble can change them later. Worth a word with Noble before it ships.
options: Similar within ±10%; smaller or bigger 10–25%; much past 25%

questions.q: Where do the six tags outside Noble's four groups go?
questions.context:
What this is about. No outdoor space, 6+ months, Full service, Renovated, Water views and New development fit none of Noble's groups (NW-045).

Why it needs you. The server rejects a tag no longer on the list, so renaming or dropping one needs a data migration. Keeping every current string avoids it.
options: Similarities for Full service, Renovated, Water views, New development; a "Differences" group for No outdoor space and 6+ months
Drop the ones a feature or check already says
needs a migration of stored tags

questions.q: Should the five-row price table also go in the email?
questions.context:
What this is about. The price table on Findings runs 10 to 12 rows and confused Noble. The replacement is five rows (low, three inner points, high) plus a calculator (NW-065).

Why it needs you. The email uses the same rows today (Frankie's full steps). One table everywhere is easier to explain, and the writer and QA then check what the agent saw.
options: Five rows on Findings and in the email
Five on Findings, the full steps in the email
Five everywhere, full steps behind a "more rows" link on Findings

questions.q: Should Hubert see the agent's own number and the target after the reveal?
questions.short: Hubert sees the target and your call
questions.context:
What this is about. D-4 said Hubert sees the target once the result is shown. The build never shows it (NW-068, NW-093). The fix is a new prompt version. The numbers are computed without the target either way, and the writer stays blind.

Why it needs you. D-4 covers only the target. The agent sees their own Gate number beside the estimate, and Hubert could use it to explain the gap.
options: read-only; never in the email or the writer

questions.q: Whose number is the target by default?
questions.context:
What this is about. A new toggle says whose the target is: client, agent or both (NW-070). The label follows it.

Why it needs you. The field already reads as the client's hope, and Noble read it that way.

questions.q: Pre-approval: yes or no, or yes or no plus the amount?
questions.context:
What this is about. The client fields (NW-074) add financing (cash or mortgage) and pre-approval.

Why it needs you. The amount caps what a buyer can offer, which is what Noble used to argue his all-cash offer. It costs one optional field.
options: Yes or no, plus the amount

questions.q: Which good email is the example, and who writes it?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble wants a good email agents can look at (NW-085). It later serves Sort notes and headlines too.

Why it needs you. It sets the bar for Casa's voice. The Barclay sample uses the engine's own numbers; Noble approves the voice. It needs the writer's real eval run, which waits on TD-3's key.
options: The 100 Barclay sample, drafted by the writer, edited by Noble
You write one by hand against the sample's numbers

questions.q: May an agent mark a report as sent without using the Copy button?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble could not reach Done (NW-086). Mark as sent only turns on after a copy through the button. A hand copy from the textarea never does.

Why it needs you. Allowing it changes a rule you set. The copy log would still record only real copies.
options: Yes, Mark as sent always works
No, a button copy comes first

questions.q: What may Hubert write on the platform?
questions.context:
What this is about. Hubert is read-only now. You want him to see what the agent sees and maybe act (NW-093).

Why it needs you. D-27 item 6 says he never tiers, writes notes or picks tags. B keeps that and still gives him real ability. C weakens the notes, which are the agent's own learning. The confirmation card goes to Claude Design.
options: Propose and confirm: home and comp facts, features, putting a removed export row back, email fixes
B plus proposing tags and notes

questions.q: Who writes "How Hubert got there"?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble found it dense (NW-063). Today it is built in code from the engine's output, not by a model.

Why it needs you. Every figure must come from the engine, the screen is opened constantly, and a model call adds cost and delay. An "Ask Hubert about this" chip can open the drawer instead.

What it blocks. Dispatch 21 item 1 builds on A; B moves the item to Calliste.
options: Hubert's live words from a model call

questions.q: Does the writer move to Calliste, the new AI track?
questions.context:
What this is about. You defined Calliste as owner of all AI prompts, tools and context (NW-093 a). It takes Hubert. The writer (Dispatch 13 phase 2) is also a Claude call with a prompt and an eval.

Why it needs you. Splitting AI work across two tracks recreates the problem Calliste is for. Mason keeps Send UI, QA and fair-housing. Calliste starts after the account move.
options: Yes, Calliste owns the writer's prompts and eval
No, the writer stays with Mason

questions.q: Should deal terms (seller target, price, rate, down payment) reach Hubert after the reveal?
questions.context:
What this is about. They are kept out today as a seller's target is a deal term (NW-068).

Why it needs you. Decide with the client fields (NW-074) so privacy and the fair-housing limits are set once.
options: Include them after the reveal, same rule as the target

questions.q: How should sessions read production data?
questions.context:
What this is about. You want Claude sessions to see what happens in production (NW-090). The rule today is that sessions never connect to the production database.

Why it needs you. A key-gated inspection API keeps the rule. It is read-only at the database (its own select-only actor), returns named views with client text redacted, and shows client text only for one report at a time, logged before it returns, at most 20 an hour. A separate test key lets a session write, but only as a test user, and copies of real reports are always redacted. A read-only database role is better for ad hoc SQL but breaks the rule. A needs four settings (TD-14) and runs from Casa's account only (Dispatch 23 items 3–4).
options: redacted by default; text on request, logged

questions.q: Should mentors see every agent's report, or only their own agents'?
questions.context:
What this is about. Admins can open any report by link, but only the owner's reports are listed, and mentors are admitted nowhere (NW-088).

Why it needs you. There are two or three mentors; assignment needs someone to maintain it, and we don't build on agent responsiveness. Agents would be told in their welcome copy that mentors can read their reports. Until then: open Noble's report from its ?report= link.

What it holds. Deploying Dispatch 22a gives every mentor read access to every report, so Casanova holds 22a's merge until you answer. B changes one rule, in two places. The sign-in fix (22 item 2) can ship on its own first.

questions.q: Who may start and reset a sample report?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble and Kara review flows and can't use the sample today (NW-054). A co-op sample is added.

Why it needs you. Replies and Hubert's transcript can't be deleted, so a truly clean reset means a new report from the same code and the old one archived (new link).

Until you answer, the server keeps samples admin-only. A widens it to mentors (Dispatch 23 items 1–2).
options: Admins and mentors; reset replaces the report
Admins only; reset replaces the report
Admins and mentors; try an in-place reset

questions.q: When do the Phase A dispatches start, given the move to Casa's Claude account?
questions.short: Dispatch before or after the move
questions.context:
What this is about. Sessions can't move between Claude accounts (NW-096). Mason, Abacus and Surveyor already run in this account; they can take Dispatches 15–22 now and restart in the Casa account later from kickoffs, as they did on 2026-10-13. A new track (Calliste, Dispatch 24) and anything that holds a production key (Dispatch 23) start in the Casa account.

Why it needs you. Starting now gets the build moving while you design; holding everything costs about a week.
options: Running tracks start now; new tracks and production keys wait for the Casa account

questions.q: How do we record the next walk-through?
questions.context:
What this is about. The last walk-through wasn't recorded; the dictation is all we have (NW-097).

Why it needs you. It costs nothing to record on your own machine. The activity log (NW-099) only shows what Noble did, not what he said.
options: Record on your machine (screen and mic)
Upgrade the Meet host seat to one with recording
activity log and notebook notes only

questions.q: A rental-comps report: wanted, and when?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble comped rentals for a client buying to rent out (NW-021). Today the tool warns when a pasted link is a rental, which he liked. A rental-comps report would take rentals and warn on sales instead, and needs the engine to price rents: a new report kind.

Why it needs you. It's a real use, but not the pilot's core. Today's gate stays either way.
options: Later: after the pilot's sales flow settles
Soon: investor clients are part of the pilot

questions.q: Create the email as a Gmail draft, for Casa Workspace accounts?
questions.context:
What this is about. NW-102. A Google Cloud project under Casa's Workspace, its OAuth consent set to Internal, asks Casa users once for Gmail's compose permission (no Google app review for internal apps). On "Create Gmail draft" the browser gets a short-lived token and puts the Designed email straight into the agent's Drafts, built exactly as it should arrive: no paste problems (left-aligned, italic, blue links). No Gmail tokens stored. Casa Workspace accounts only; personal Gmail keeps Copy. The same Casa Google client also lets Workspace trust the comp report's Google sign-in (Noble's refusal).

Why it needs you. You create the project and client in Casa's Workspace admin (a checklist comes with the dispatch). Build is Phase B.
options: Yes: set up the Casa Google client, build it in Phase B
Not now: Copy stays the only way

topics.title: The design port
topics.intro: The design port merged in #77 and is live. You confirmed DP-1 to DP-8 as built (DP-6 with free-text tags too). Two questions from Mason's PR:

questions.q: After Noble: keep Co-op as the default type?
questions.context: Mason's finding in #77: the engine counts like for like, so a co-op report counts no condo comps, and most Tribeca homes are condos. Sort and Findings say so and offer Make this report a condo in one click, which carries the demo. Options for after: default to Condo, or read the type from the home's listing.

questions.q: A full agent's why on the Gate: optional?
questions.context: The handoff makes it optional for graduated (full) agents, and the build does that. New (practice) agents must write 100+ characters.

settled: DP-3 · Findings locked until every comp is done: recorded 2026-10-15.

topics.title: The comp report
topics.intro: The comp report is priority one. These come from D-25 and D-17, from the writer's PR (#76) and from Jev's PR (#56).

questions.q: Who reviews the fair-housing list?
questions.context:
What this is about. The writer's QA has one hard block: compliance (D-2). A term on the hard list blocks Copy outright ("adults only", "perfect for young professionals", "no Section 8", "school district", "safe neighborhood"). A word on the near list ("family", "church", "school") warns, and the agent acknowledges it before copying.

Why it needs you. Mason drafted the list from HUD's advertising guidance and New York City's Human Rights Law ({repo}/tools-src/comp-report/workspace/fair-housing.ts, version fh-2026-10-14). A list that blocks agents' emails needs a reviewer before the pilot widens.

questions.q: "Appraisal contingency": keep it blocked, or allow it as a deal term?
questions.context:
What this is about. "Appraisal" in client copy is a hard block (design §9.3), because a comp email must never read as an appraisal. So an agent who writes about waiving the appraisal contingency in the next step can't copy the email.

Why it needs you. The phrase is a normal deal term in a buyer's offer. Allowing it means one exception in the list; keeping it means agents rephrase.
options: Allow the phrase as a deal term

questions.q: Does the writer's house voice read right?
questions.context:
What this is about. Claude now drafts the headlines and the email's sections in Casa's voice, in Frankie's order. The voice is a short style file: plain words, specific comparisons, numbers only from the comps, one to three lines a comp. It's quoted in full in #76's description ({repo}/tools-src/comp-report/server/house-voice.ts).

Why it needs you. It's Casa's voice in front of clients. The real eval drafts (100 Barclay and Frankie's #517) come once CR_EVAL_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is in the cloud environment (TD-3); read them together if you'd rather.
options: Wait for the eval drafts first

questions.q: Jev's seven questions: go with them as written?
questions.context:
What this is about. Jev answers seven fixed questions about each listing's text (sponsor sale, estate sale, tenant in place and the like). The wording is at the end of #56's description. Phase 2 goes live on the reviewed text.

Why it needs you. Casanova read them and found nothing to change. A change after the labelled batch runs means running it again.

questions.q: The ±3 floor band and the ½-mile distance flag most comps. What now?
questions.short: Floor band and distance thresholds: keep?
questions.context:
What this is about. The floor band (±3, from Frankie's email) flags 8 of Hannah's 11 comps; Kara's ½ mile flags 6 of the sample's 11, five of them Primary. A flag is a prompt to the agent, never a block.

Why it needs you. Noble sets or confirms them. Until he does, the numbers stand.
options: Keep them until Noble weighs in
say to what in the note

questions.q: Counsel's two questions: who do they go to, and when?
questions.context:
What this is about. Surveyor found two legal questions research can't settle: (1) is a CMA an "appraisal" under New York law? (2) in sponsor sales, does transfer tax the buyer pays count toward the taxable consideration? Both are in {repo}/docs/comp-report/research/adjustments.md, with sources.

Why it needs you. (1) matters before the pilot; (2) only if the tool ever computes the sponsor arithmetic.
options: Hold until the pilot is near
Send them to a closing attorney now

topics.title: Profile pics
topics.intro: Painter's roster (Dispatch 12, phase 1) is merged in #71. Phase 2 imports the roster once.

questions.q: Where do agents' contact details come from for the roster's import?
questions.short: D-24: the signatures doc or FileMaker?
questions.context:
What this is about. The roster imports about 110 agents once: names, titles, emails and phones. The email-signatures Google Doc has duplicates, likely typos and gaps.

Why it needs you. If a system of record (FileMaker) sits behind the doc, the import reads an export of that instead of parsing a doc.

settled: PP-2 · Already-filed photos: placed or to do?: recorded 2026-10-15.

questions.q: Agent photos and renames inside the studio (blocking posts now)
questions.context:
The feedback (Oct 9). An easy way to add or replace an agent's photo and edit their library name in Creative Studio. Missing photos are blocking posts: Arianna Fotinos's new photo, Emma C. to Emma L. (Emma Liuzzi) with an updated photo, and Jackie Tran, who has none and two Greenpoint closings waiting.

questions.q: Instagram handles on each agent's record
questions.context: The feedback (Oct 9). Captions go out with name placeholders because there's no handle list anywhere. Once handles live on the agent record, the post builders could output a ready-to-paste tag line.
options: The roster gets the field now (Painter); tag lines in the builders later (Publisher)
With the CMS, when Concierge starts

questions.q: In Contract: the one-agent slide header
questions.context: The feedback (Oct 8). "IN CONTRACT: FRANKIE D." next to "IN CONTRACT: MORNINGSIDE HEIGHTS" reads inconsistently, and the name is already on the photo. Allow a neighborhood or free-text header like two-agent mode, or a layout that doesn't need one.

questions.q: Keep the StreetEasy link with each property, in every builder
questions.short: Keep the StreetEasy link per property
questions.context: The feedback (Oct 8). Store the StreetEasy URL on each deal, show it as a link in the editor, keep it in saved sessions and exports, in the In Contract, Closed, Listing and Editorial builders.

questions.q: Editorial builder: a caption generator, slide-filling instructions for the AI, end-slide layouts
questions.context:
The feedback (Aug 28). A native Instagram caption generator; instructions so the AI fills each slide with the right photos and captions; a toggle for end-slide layouts.

Note. The retiring Editorial session found the builder works in a sandbox; Publisher's first job there is one live run ({repo}/docs/parked/sessions/editorial-builder.md).
options: Queue it for Publisher, after the live run

questions.q: Business card: "How do you upload your headshot?"
questions.context: The feedback (June, no name). An agent expected a headshot on the business card. The card has no headshot, by design.
options: Won't fix: the card has no headshot
Add a headshot to the card

topics.title: Moving to Casa accounts
topics.intro: Erez asked for Casa-owned accounts once the comp report settles (D-26). Settled so far: casacalliste@gmail.com stays Casa's identity, made Casa-held; the Post Log is the caption tracker the builders link to.

questions.q: Move the API keys that process client data to Casa accounts before the pilot widens?
questions.short: API keys to Casa before the pilot?
questions.context:
What this is about. Anthropic, the AI Gateway (Jev) and Firecrawl process comp report data. Moving them is independent of GitHub and Claude: new key, set it in Netlify, redeploy, revoke the old one.

Why it needs you. It means Casa accounts and a Casa card for three services before the rest of the move.
options: and every new key is made on a Casa account from now
With everything else, after the comp report

questions.q: Which Claude plan does Casa buy, and who's the second admin?
questions.context:
What this is about. It needs Projects, memory, connectors, artifacts with databases, the desktop app and Claude Code cloud sessions, with enough usage for parallel tracks. Signed in with casacalliste, so it survives any one person.

Why it needs you. Erez pays; a seat with less headroom than today slows the tracks.

questions.q: Erez's line on the two accounts
questions.short: What Casa info your personal Claude may see
questions.context: The proposal. Status and planning readable from your personal Claude, through the repo; client data, agents' details and comp reports stay in Casa's account. After the move, Casa data is cleaned out of the personal account.

questions.q: The Casa desk artifact: move it, or keep it personal?
questions.short: The Casa desk: move or keep?
questions.context: What this is about. It was built to be private to you. In a Casa-owned account, assume Casa's admins can see it.
options: Move it, and keep it work-only
Keep it personal, with no client or agent data in it

questions.q: What stays yours?
questions.context: What this is about. Patterns you reuse elsewhere (the tool design system approach, the dispatch method, skill structure) can be kept as a personal copy. If your contractor agreement says anything about IP, that governs: check it rather than assume.

questions.q: Who's the second owner on the GitHub organization and each service account?
questions.context: What this is about. So Casa's tools don't depend on one person's logins: GitHub, Netlify, Anthropic, Vercel, Firecrawl, the Claude account and casacalliste's recovery.

questions.q: Is the GitHub Pages copy of the studio still used?
questions.context: What this is about. Its address changes with the repo and doesn't redirect. agents/SCHEMA.md and the functions' CORS note name kjcamron.github.io.
options: No: turn it off before the move
Yes: keep it, and update its address

topics.title: Your to-dos
topics.intro: Settings and errands only you can do. Mark one Done when it's done; anything left here is still to do. Never paste a key into a chat.

questions.q: Label the 30 listings for Jev's calibration
questions.context: About 20 minutes, and Hannah could do it. The sheet is {repo}/docs/comp-report/jev-labels.csv; how to fill it in is {repo}/docs/comp-report/jev-calibration.md. Don't look at any Jev output first. If a link won't open, say so in its note.

questions.q: Walk the comp report on production
questions.context: Make a new comp from 100 Barclay #17L's link, add five comps by link and confirm them, tier and note them on Sort, give your number on Findings, then pick a headline and copy the email on Send. Leave notes with Ctrl+. as you go. Now the writer is in (#76), try Write it on Send too.

questions.q: Confirm CR-1's step 6 in Netlify's function log
questions.context: Logs → Functions → identity-signup (or identity-validate): find one line with "allowed":false from your Gmail test. No session can read those logs.

questions.q: Delete the samplepics branch
questions.context: D-16 said delete it. Sessions can't delete branches (the proxy refuses), so it's yours on GitHub.

questions.q: Sit down with Noble
questions.short: Noble: glossary, thresholds, the differences approach
questions.context: Three things for one meeting: the glossary draft's 8 open questions ({repo}/docs/comp-report/research/glossary-draft.md, updated in #70); the thresholds in CR-5; and the "differences between comps" approach (design §6.6), which builds on his point that prices already carry their features.

questions.q: Brand the Google sign-in (optional)
questions.context: Google's screen says "Netlify Identity" because sign-in uses Netlify's default client. To make it say Casa Blanca, paste a Google Cloud client's ID and secret into Netlify → Identity → Registration → External providers → Google. Best done on Casa's Google account, with the move (D-26).

questions.q: Record the next walk-through with Noble
questions.context: Screen and mic, on your machine, per NB-26. Share the file or transcript in the repo's feedback folder.

questions.q: Add the inspect and test keys to the cloud environment
questions.context: The three settings are in Netlify (Production). What's left: add CR_INSPECT_KEY and CR_TEST_KEY to this Claude Code environment, with the same values as in Netlify (they're in your password manager). They do nothing until Dispatch 23 items 3–4 land. To switch the inspection off, unset CR_INSPECT_KEY in Netlify and redeploy.

questions.q: Pick a co-op and pull its StreetEasy export for the co-op sample
questions.context: A real co-op sale with comps near it, exported the way the 100 Barclay one was. Put it where Mason can read it (the sources folder). Needed for the co-op sample and for reviewing the co-op flow (NW-054, NW-066).

questions.q: Invite a second address and check the sign-in works
questions.short: Test an invite end to end
questions.context: After Mason's fix for "We couldn't check your access" lands (NW-091), invite one real second address, accept the invite, and confirm you get in with no sign-out first. Tell Casanova if it fails.

questions.q: Ask Noble to confirm the size-scale bands
questions.context: Show Noble NB-10's bands (similar within 10%, smaller or bigger to 25%, much past that) and tell Casanova if he wants them different.

questions.q: Swap the Anthropic key in Make
questions.context: Make has one Anthropic connection, My Anthropic Claude connection, and the live Mailchimp ISO Blast Automation (every 15 minutes) uses it in its three Claude steps. In Casa's Anthropic workspace, make a key just for it (say make-iso-blast). In Make, go to Connections, find that connection, choose Reauthorize, and paste the new key. Watch one run go through, then revoke the old key in your personal console.
